the structure of the PorBIA porin from N. gonorrhaeae in complex with ATP and phosphate reveals a surplus of positive charge inside the porin channel and that the arginine residue Arg92 is essential for bacterial invasion into host cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the structural basis of the phosphate-dependent invasion mechanism of Neisseria gonorrhae.
the structure and function of a channel-forming protein, which is associated with disseminating gonorrhoeae and which is involved in the invasion process of host cells.
the structural and functional characterization of the PorBIA porin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Arg92 in PorBIA is essential for the invasion of host cells and that this function is supported by a surplus of positive charge in the channel.
the structure-function analysis of the PorBIA porin revealed that the positive charge inside the channel, the L3 loop and the β2-bulge are important for the function of the protein.
the unique structure of PorB is responsible for the rapid bacterial invasion into epithelial cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structure and function relationship of porins from Neisseriacea is complex and requires a more detailed analysis.
the structure of PorB from N. gonorrhaeae is a phosphate- and ATP-binding porin that is unique in disseminating bacteria and may therefore contribute to the rapid invasion of the host.
PorBIA has a unique structure and function that is not present in other Neisseria species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structure of the channel-forming porins from Neisseria species is highly conserved.

we have determined the structure of the gonococcal porin PorBIA in a complex with phosphate and ATP, which provides insights into the molecular mechanism of the phosphate-dependent invasion into human cells.
the structure of PorB is a good model for explaining the molecular mechanisms of host cell invasion.
